messages:
deploy-bot: deploy started: release/2026-03-18/runtime-heuristics-2 -> canary sched
maya: seeing p99 jump on canary, +220ms vs baseline :grimacing:
vikram: confirmed. p95 flat-ish but p99 tails up. grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abc/runtime-p99?var=canary
maya: rolling-out only 5% canary right? how bad is it on that slice?
cheng: 5% canary. digging into kernel-selector logs now
oliver: quick metric: average microbatch size on canary dropped from 4.1 -> 1.8 per GPU
sara: that lines up with the spike. smaller microbatches => lower throughput but can increase tail latency due to queueing weirdness
vikram: any config flips in this change? commit 7f3b2a added new 'tiny_batch_bias' heuristic
cheng: yep that heuristic prefers lower batching for short-seq traffic to reduce median latency. looks like it mis-classifies many requests as short-seq
maya: misclassification -> more small batches -> more KV cache churn?
oliver: KV cache eviction rate on canary is +3.8x. logs showing frequent cache misses and extra KV fetches
sara: paste of kernel-selector debug output:
```
[2026-03-18T15:02:01Z] selector: seq_len=32 predicted_short=true bias_score=0.87 chosen_microbatch=1
[2026-03-18T15:02:01Z] kvcache: miss key=conv:12345
```
vikram: also seeing pipeline stalls in runtime traces. p99 spans include extra 60-120ms KV fetch latencies
maya: is the heuristic threshold a single number? can we flip it while keeping rest of rollout?
cheng: it's a model + threshold combo, baked into the kernel-selection binary. changing realtime requires full redeploy of canary tier
oliver: for a quick mitigation, we could force microbatch_min=3 via runtime config override for canary nodes
vikram: try it on canary. if microbatch_min prevents tiny batches maybe KV churn falls
maya: pushed override config to canary: microbatch_min=3
deploy-bot: config override applied to canary nodes (5%)
oliver: metrics 3m after override: microbatch size climbed to ~3.2, KV evictions down ~45%
maya: p99 trending down now but still above baseline by ~30ms
sara: looks like improvement but not enough. we should consider rollback of the selector change if it doesn't converge quickly
vikram: agree. can we revert just the selector binary to previous stable? that’s a straight rollback of the canary
cheng: prepared revert PR: revert(7f3b2a). ready to apply if we hit another plateau in 10m
maya: +1 to revert if p99 doesn't return to baseline in next 10m
oliver: new observation: requests with short system-instr tokens are being mis-classified due to tokenizer change from another PR
sara: ugh cross-PR interaction. that increases revert urgency
maya: current p99 delta now ~18ms above baseline after override, but trending flat
vikram: decision: initiate canary revert now to be safe. execute revert and monitor
revert-bot: initiating revert: revert/7f3b2a -> canary
deploy-bot: revert deployed to canary (5%). monitoring window started
oliver: within 2 minutes microbatch size back to 4.0 and KV evictions stable
maya: p99 on canary back to baseline within 6 minutes :tada:
sara: rollback success. nice rapid decisioning team
cheng: leaving the revert PR open with notes about tokenizer interaction and selector thresholds
vikram: action items: 1) add unit tests for tokenizer->selector mapping; 2) make selector heuristic feature-flagged and remotely adjustable; 3) postmortem in #postmortems
maya: I'll write a short incident timeline and drop it in #postmortems. include Grafana snapshots and the debug logs
oliver: also recommend a staging canary job that replays representative short/long sequences to catch misclassification
maya: thanks everyone. putting this to 'resolved' for now, will follow up with postmortem tomorrow
vikram: kudos to folks for quick mitigation and rollback :clap:
revert-bot: revert successful, canary stable
deploy-bot: note: no customer-facing errors observed during canary, only internal latency SLO deviation
maya: OK closing thread. follow-ups tracked in backlog ticket INF-2481"
